desktop.actual_sources_citation_text:
Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the Earliest Period to the Present Time. Vol. 1. Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1884. compiled secondary (Andreas) source · not archived
"Fort Dearborn History." Chicagology. Reprinting the address delivered by Hon. John Wentworth at the Fort Dearborn Memorial Tablet ceremonies, 21 May 1881, as printed in the Chicago Tribune, 22 May 1881; with the caption to a woodcut of Alexander Hesler's 1855 photograph, an addendum on the fort in 1850 signed Robert Fergus, and an extract from Chicago Magazine, Vol. 1, No. 1, March 1857. later scholarship source · archived
what this source supplies, and does not
'Bird’s-Eye View of Old Fort Dearborn.' Illustration at p. 27 of J. Seymour Currey, The Story of Old Fort Dearborn (Chicago: A. C. McClurg & Co., 1912). Numbered reconstruction of the first fort, not a contemporary view. modern retrospective illustration/reconstruction source · archived
what this source supplies, and does not
Kurz & Allison. Chicago In Early Days, 1779-1857. Chicago: Kurz & Allison, 76 & 78 Wabash Avenue, 1893. Chromolithograph, fifteen numbered vignettes with printed key. modern retrospective illustration/reconstruction source · not archived
what this source supplies, and does not
Quaife, Milo Milton. Chicago and the Old Northwest, 1673-1835: A Study of the Evolution of the Northwestern Frontier, together with a History of Fort Dearborn. Chicago: University of Chicago Press, 1913. later scholarship source · archived
what this source supplies, and does not
"Journal of Lieutenant James Strode Swearingen", printed as Appendix I in Milo Milton Quaife, Chicago and the Old Northwest, 1673-1835: A Study of the Evolution of the Northwestern Frontier, together with a History of Fort Dearborn (Chicago: University of Chicago Press, 1913), pp. 373-377. The Chicago entry, Wednesday 17 August 1803, runs across pp. 376-377. period/eyewitness source · not archived

reprints Journal of Lieutenant James Strode Swearingen, kept on the march from Detroit to Chicago in temporary command of the company sent to establish the first Fort Dearborn; entry for Wednesday 17 August 1803, the day of arrival 1803-08-17

what this source supplies, and does not
Whistler, Captain John. "Fort Dearborn" [draught of the garrison and its vicinity], dated in the parade 'January 25th 1808', with its 'Index annexed to the Draught of Fort Dearborn &c.' signed at Fort Dearborn 20 February 1808. Original in the files of the War Department, Washington. Reproduced as the plate 'Fort Dearborn and Vicinity in 1808. From the original draft by Captain Whistler in the archives of the War Department at Washington', facing p. 164 of Quaife, Chicago and the Old Northwest, 1673-1835 (Chicago, 1913); the index is printed in full in note 413 on the same pages. period/eyewitness source · archived
what this source supplies, and does not
